unit.title: The Pro Game
unit.summary: Tours (PPA, MLP, APP), event formats, team format and DreamBreaker, world rankings, pro styles, reading a pro point.

payload.prompt: Match each pickleball tour to its format.

pairs.definition: Individual pro tournament circuit with brackets, slams, and world rankings.
Team-based league with franchises, rosters, and a DreamBreaker tiebreak.
Association of Pickleball Players circuit mixing pro and amateur brackets.
United Pickleball Association, the umbrella over the PPA and MLP.

explanation.summary: PPA is individual events, MLP is teams, APP bridges pro and amateur play, and the UPA sits over the PPA and MLP. The APP is its own tour.
explanation.sayThisLine: PPA is individual, MLP is teams, APP mixes pros and amateurs, and UPA is the umbrella.

payload.prompt: PPA Tour is a team-based league. True?

explanation.correct: PPA is a circuit of individual tournaments: players and partners enter brackets. MLP is the team league.
explanation.incorrect: PPA events are brackets where players and partners enter as individuals. Teams and franchises belong to MLP.
explanation.sayThisLine: PPA is the individual tour. MLP is the team league.

payload.prompt: Match MLP terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: A team in Major League Pickleball that owns a roster and plays in the season.
A competition between two franchises with four games (women's, men's, mixed x2).
The annual competition where franchises play matches and compete for a title.

explanation.summary: In MLP, franchises are the teams, a match is several games between two franchises, and the season is the yearly run toward a title.
explanation.sayThisLine: Franchise is the team. Match is four games. Season is the run to the title.

payload.prompt: Complete the tour-structure statement.
payload.template: The {{umbrella}} sits over the PPA and MLP, while the {{separate}} is its own tour.

explanation.correct: The UPA is the umbrella over the PPA and MLP. The APP runs its own separate circuit of events.
explanation.incorrect: The UPA is the umbrella body over the PPA and MLP. The APP, the Association of Pickleball Players, is a separate tour.
explanation.sayThisLine: The UPA covers the PPA and MLP. The APP does its own thing.

lessons.title: How a pro event works
lessons.objective: Follow a bracket, a slam and points.

payload.prompt: What determines who plays whom in a pro bracket?

options.text: Seeding and ranking; top seeds are placed so they meet late.
Players choose their opponents.
Alphabetical order by last name.
Whoever arrives at the venue first.

explanation.correct: Players are seeded by ranking, and the bracket is arranged so the top seeds do not meet until the later rounds.
explanation.incorrect: Brackets are built from seeding. The strongest players are spread apart so the biggest matchups come late.
explanation.sayThisLine: Top seeds are spread out, so the big matchups come late.

payload.prompt: Order the stages of a typical pro pickleball event.

explanation.sayThisLine: Draw, rounds, semis, final, winner. The tournament arc.
explanation.correct: Events flow from bracket release, through rounds, to a champion.
explanation.incorrect: Tournaments flow from bracket release through rounds, with each round trimming the field, until one team is left.

payload.prompt: Two events, one week apart. Why do pros circle the slam?

situation.narrative: A pro is planning her schedule around a slam and a regular event.

facts.label: Ranking impact
facts.value: Slams usually award the most points

options.label: Prioritize the slam: more points and more prestige
options.consequence: Right. Slams usually offer the most ranking points and the biggest spotlight, so pros plan around them.
considerations: A win there carries extra prestige

options.label: Prioritize the regular event: an easier field
options.consequence: An easier field can help, but the points and spotlight are smaller. Most pros still plan around the slams.

payload.expertNote: Slams are the majors, so they usually carry the most ranking points and the biggest spotlight. Check each tour's own points table for the exact numbers.

payload.prompt: Match pro event terms to their definitions.

pairs.definition: The tournament structure showing who plays whom and in what order.
Ranking players 1 (best) through N to determine bracket placement.
The official bracket announced before the event starts.

explanation.summary: The bracket is the structure, seeding decides who goes where, and the draw is the published bracket.
explanation.sayThisLine: Bracket is the structure, seeding is the rank, and the draw is the published bracket.

payload.prompt: Complete the slam event statement.
payload.template: A {{event}} is a {{type}} pro event that awards {{points}} ranking points.

explanation.correct: Slams are the majors, and they usually carry the most ranking points.
explanation.incorrect: A slam is a major event. Majors usually award the most ranking points and attract the strongest fields.
explanation.sayThisLine: A slam is a major, so it's big points and a big field.

lessons.title: MLP: teams and DreamBreaker
lessons.objective: Follow the four-game match and DreamBreaker.

payload.prompt: What are the four games in an MLP match?

options.text: Women's doubles, men's doubles, mixed doubles, mixed doubles.
Singles, singles, doubles, doubles.
Three-on-three, two-on-two, one-on-one, exhibition.
Whatever the two teams agree on that day.

explanation.correct: An MLP match is women's doubles, men's doubles, then two mixed doubles games.
explanation.incorrect: The match structure is fixed: women's doubles, men's doubles, mixed, mixed. It is all doubles, no singles.
explanation.sayThisLine: Four games: women's, men's, mixed, mixed. Then maybe a DreamBreaker.

payload.prompt: Order the events in an MLP match.

explanation.sayThisLine: Women's, men's, mixed, mixed, then the tally. If it's 2-2, DreamBreaker.
explanation.correct: MLP matches play women's, men's, then two mixed games, then tally the score.
explanation.incorrect: MLP matches play in a set order: women's, men's, mixed, mixed. Only a 2-2 tie goes to the DreamBreaker.

payload.prompt: A DreamBreaker only happens if the match is tied 2-2. True?

choices.label: Yes, at 2-2 it goes to DreamBreaker

explanation.correct: The DreamBreaker breaks the tie when a match is 2-2 after four games.
explanation.incorrect: The DreamBreaker is the tiebreak, and it only happens when teams are tied 2-2. A team that wins three games is done.
explanation.sayThisLine: DreamBreaker is the tiebreaker at 2-2. If one team leads, they win.

payload.prompt: Match MLP tiebreak terms to their meanings.

pairs.definition: An MLP rally-scoring tiebreak game to 21 when a match is 2-2.
Every rally scores a point for the winner, not just the serving side.
A team's position in the league table based on its results over the season.

explanation.summary: The DreamBreaker is the rally-scored tiebreak for a 2-2 match, and standings rank the teams over the season.
explanation.sayThisLine: DreamBreaker is rally scoring to 21, and the winner takes the match.

payload.prompt: Complete the MLP match statement.
payload.template: An MLP match has {{count}} games before any DreamBreaker: women's doubles, men's doubles and {{mixed}} mixed doubles games.

explanation.correct: Four games: one women's, one men's and two mixed. That is how a match can end 2-2 and need a DreamBreaker.
explanation.incorrect: It is four games: women's doubles, men's doubles and two mixed doubles. Two games each is how a 2-2 tie can happen.
explanation.sayThisLine: Four games, two of them mixed. Tied 2-2 means DreamBreaker.

lessons.title: Scoring at the pro level
lessons.objective: Know when pros use side-out vs rally.

payload.prompt: Do all pro pickleball events use the same scoring system?

options.text: No; formats vary by tour and event, and they can change.
Yes, all pros play rally scoring.
Yes, all pros play side-out.
It depends on the player's preference.

explanation.correct: Tours and events choose their own formats, and those choices shift over time. MLP's DreamBreaker, for example, is rally scoring.
explanation.incorrect: There is no single pro format. Tours and events choose their own, and players do not get a vote on the day.
explanation.sayThisLine: Scoring depends on the tour and the event, so I'd check which format they're using.

payload.prompt: In side-out scoring, the receiving team can score when they win a rally. True?

choices.label: No, they only gain serve, not points

explanation.correct: In side-out scoring only the serving side scores. Receivers who win the rally win the serve, not a point.
explanation.incorrect: Side-out means the serving team scores when it wins a rally, while the receiving team only gains the serve.
explanation.sayThisLine: In side-out, you have to be serving to score.

payload.prompt: The scoreboard at a pro match looks different from her home court. Your move?

situation.narrative: You are watching a pro match with her and the scoring does not look like what she plays locally.

facts.label: Fact
facts.value: Formats vary by tour and event

options.label: Ask which scoring format this event uses
options.consequence: She lights up. Different tours and events use different formats, and asking shows you are curious, not guessing.
considerations: Formats vary by tour and event
You avoid a confident wrong guess

options.label: Assume it works like her home court
options.consequence: Risky. The event may use rally scoring or another format, and you would confidently misread the score.
considerations: Pro formats can differ from rec play

options.label: Say the scoreboard must be broken
options.consequence: The board is fine. It is just a different format, and blaming it makes you look like you did not pay attention.
considerations: A different format is more likely

payload.expertNote: Pro formats vary by tour and event and are changing, so check the event page or ask rather than assuming. Rally scoring is one option you will see.

payload.prompt: Match scoring system to its key rule.

pairs.definition: Only the serving team scores; receivers must win serve first.
Every rally awards a point to the winner, regardless of who served.
The rules that determine when and how players score points in a match.

explanation.summary: Side-out: only the serving side scores. Rally: the rally winner always scores. The scoring format is the tour's or event's choice.
explanation.sayThisLine: Side-out means serve to score. Rally means every rally counts.

payload.prompt: Complete the pro scoring statement.
payload.template: In {{scoring}}, every rally scores a point; in {{sideout}}, only {{side}} scores.

explanation.correct: Rally scoring: every rally gives a point to its winner. Side-out: only the serving side can score.
explanation.incorrect: The two systems differ on who can score. In rally scoring it is the rally winner, in side-out it is only the serving side.
explanation.sayThisLine: Rally scoring counts every rally. Side-out counts only the serving side.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: That player is a total dinker, just dinks everything.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: They play soft, patient dinking rallies instead of hitting hard.
They're bad at pickleball.
They only play in doubles.
They use a cheap paddle.

payload.translation: A dinker is a player who wins with soft, patient kitchen rallies instead of power.

followUps.line: So they wait for someone to pop the ball up?
followUps.why: Checks your understanding of the strategy without judging it.

followUps.line: Patience and soft hands can beat power, right?
followUps.why: Shows respect for the style and invites her take.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Dinkers are strategists who win through control, not pace. Ask what she likes about watching them.

payload.prompt: What is a pro 'banger' known for?

options.text: Hitting hard and fast to win points with power.
Playing only at the net.
Serving every time.
Winning every match.

explanation.correct: Bangers speed the ball up, forcing errors or hitting winners with pace instead of waiting out the dink rally.
explanation.incorrect: A banger is a power player who hits hard and fast. It is a style, not a guarantee of winning.
explanation.sayThisLine: Banger means power hitter. Dinker means patience player. Both can win.

payload.prompt: At the kitchen, a banger hits hard at a soft dink. What likely happens?

situation.narrative: Two pro styles clash at the net.

facts.label: Risk
facts.value: Hitting down on a low ball

options.label: The banger likely pops it up or nets it
options.consequence: Right. A low ball gives no room to hit down, so a hard swing often pops up or nets.
considerations: Below-net balls are hard to attack

options.label: The banger hits a winner and wins the point
options.consequence: Unlikely. Low balls do not leave enough room to attack cleanly.
considerations: Bangers wait for a ball they can attack

payload.expertNote: Dinking beats banging at the net because low balls are hard to attack. Bangers wait for a higher ball, then speed up.

payload.prompt: Match pro style to its play pattern.

pairs.definition: A power-oriented player who hits hard and fast to end rallies quickly.
A soft-game player who wins through patience, control and waiting for attackable balls.
A pro who mixes aggressive and patient shots depending on the situation.

explanation.summary: Bangers win with pace. Dinkers win with patience. Hybrids mix both, which is how most top players actually play.
explanation.sayThisLine: Banger is hard and fast. Dinker is soft and patient. Most pros mix both.

payload.prompt: Dinkers are weaker players than bangers. True?

choices.label: No, both styles win at the pro level

explanation.correct: Both styles are legitimate pro strategies, and dinkers often win through strategy and patience.
explanation.incorrect: Top pros include both bangers and dinkers. Dinkers can hit hard too; they just choose their moment.
explanation.sayThisLine: Power isn't skill. Patience wins plenty of titles.

payload.prompt: How is pro singles different from doubles?

options.text: One player per side; more running, no partner coordination.
The ball moves twice as fast.
The court is larger.
There are no kitchen rules.

explanation.correct: Singles is one-on-one, so each player covers a whole side alone and there is no partner to share the work.
explanation.incorrect: Singles uses the same court and the same kitchen rules. The difference is one player per side covering everything.
explanation.sayThisLine: Singles is one player covering the whole side. It's brutal on the legs.

payload.prompt: Singles, server has 4 points. Tap where the serve must land.

diagram.alt: Top-down pickleball court. The server is at the near end. Four service boxes: near left, near right, far left, far right.

explanation.correct: In singles the server's own score decides the side: even means serve from the right. From the near right you serve diagonally to the far left box.
explanation.incorrect: In singles the server's own score picks the side. Four is even, so she serves from the right, and every serve goes diagonally to the far left box seen from above. The kitchen is never a legal landing spot.
explanation.sayThisLine: Even score, serve from the right, aim cross-court.

payload.prompt: Pro singles matches use the full pickleball court. True?

choices.label: Yes, singles uses the full court
No, a smaller court is used

explanation.correct: Yes. Singles uses the same court with the same lines, so one player has to cover what two would in doubles.
explanation.incorrect: It is the same standard court in singles. Players just have no partner to share it with.
explanation.sayThisLine: Same court, one player. That's why singles is so tiring.

payload.prompt: She says singles is rare on tour. What is a fair way to explain why?

situation.narrative: She is telling you singles feels like a side show next to doubles.

facts.label: Pro schedules
facts.value: Doubles and mixed lead the bill

facts.label: Singles demand
facts.value: One player covers the whole side

options.label: Pickleball is doubles-first, and singles is a smaller part of the schedule
options.consequence: Fair. Most people play and watch doubles, so tours lean that way, and singles is the smaller draw.
considerations: Doubles is the default way to play

options.label: Singles is more popular, and doubles is dying
options.consequence: No. Doubles dominates at every level, so this would sound like you were making it up.
considerations: Doubles is the bread and butter

payload.expertNote: Pickleball is a doubles-first sport, and singles is a secondary format that still has real fans. Say that without putting either down.

payload.prompt: Complete the singles fact.
payload.template: Pro singles gets {{attention}} attention than doubles, and each player covers {{side}} alone.

explanation.correct: Doubles gets most of the spotlight, and in singles one player covers the entire side alone.
explanation.incorrect: Pickleball favors doubles, so singles gets less attention. With no partner, each singles player covers a whole side.
explanation.sayThisLine: Singles is one player covering a whole side. Doubles gets the spotlight.

lessons.title: Read a pro point
lessons.objective: Name what happened in a rally.

payload.prompt: The announcer says 'nice drop.' Tap where it should land.

diagram.alt: Top-down pickleball court. The hitting team is at the near end. The far side has a kitchen strip by the net, service boxes behind it and a baseline.

explanation.correct: A drop is a soft arc that lands in the far kitchen. The hitting team then walks up to the kitchen line while the ball is still in the air.
explanation.incorrect: A drop lands in the opponents' kitchen, the strip next to the net. Deep behind the kitchen gives them a ball to attack, and your own kitchen is on your side.
explanation.sayThisLine: That drop landed right in the kitchen. So they're up at the line now.

payload.prompt: Pro third shots are always drops. True?

explanation.correct: The drop is the default, but pros mix in drives when the returners are caught deep or standing flat-footed.
explanation.incorrect: The drop is the usual choice because it is consistent and lets your team move up. Pros still drive when the returners are out of position.
explanation.sayThisLine: Drop is the default. A drive is the surprise when they're caught deep.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: Did you see that reset? She flicked it back soft into the kitchen.

payload.question: What just happened?

options.text: An opponent hit a hard ball; she softly returned it to stay in play.
She won the point.
She served the ball.
She lobbed it over their heads.

payload.translation: A reset is a soft defensive shot that takes the pace off a fast ball and lands it in the kitchen.

followUps.line: So she took the speed out of it?
followUps.why: Restates what a reset does without bluffing.

followUps.line: Did that get them back to dinking?
followUps.why: Invites her to explain what happens after a reset.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Resets are defensive patience, not weakness. If you are not sure what you saw, ask her what she noticed.

payload.prompt: A fast ball comes at your kitchen. Reset or try to attack?

situation.narrative: A ball comes in faster than expected.

options.label: Reset it soft; keep the point going
options.consequence: Right. Resetting a low, fast ball keeps you in the point and takes away their attack.
considerations: A low ball is hard to attack
It often leads to a chance later

options.label: Attack it hard and end the point
options.consequence: Risky. A low, fast ball is hard to attack cleanly, so you will probably net it or pop it up.
considerations: You might hit it into the net
Or pop it up for them
A reset is the safer play

payload.expertNote: Pros reset low, fast balls. Attacking too early leads to errors.

payload.prompt: Complete the pro-point statement.
payload.template: A pro's third shot is usually a {{shot}}, so both teams get to the {{line}} and trade dinks until someone attacks.

explanation.correct: The third-shot drop buys time to move up, so the point becomes a dink rally at the kitchen line until someone finds an attackable ball.
explanation.incorrect: The usual third shot is a soft drop. It gives the serving team time to walk up, and then both teams dink at the kitchen line.
explanation.sayThisLine: Third shot drops, everybody moves up, then it's dink versus dink.

payload.prompt: What do the World Pickleball Rankings measure?

options.text: A pro player's performance in tour events, updated regularly.
How much money a player has earned.
A player's popularity on social media.
A player's age and experience.

explanation.correct: World rankings are based on tour results and the points earned at events.
explanation.incorrect: Rankings reflect competitive performance: results and points earned, not prize money or popularity.
explanation.sayThisLine: World rankings come from tour results, not from money or fame.

payload.prompt: She moved from 14th to 9th in the rankings. Places climbed?

explanation.correct: 14 minus 9 is 5. A lower number is a better ranking, so going from 14th to 9th is a five-place climb.
explanation.incorrect: Subtract the numbers: 14 minus 9 is 5. A lower number means a better ranking, so moving from 14th to 9th is a climb of five places.
explanation.sayThisLine: She jumped five spots. Nice week for her.

payload.prompt: Match ranking term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: A number (1 = best) showing a player's competitive standing based on results.
Points earned in events; more points for larger/important tournaments.
Changes in a player's position based on points earned or lost.

explanation.summary: The ranking is the position. Points are what build it. Movement is how the position changes after results.
explanation.sayThisLine: The ranking is where you stand. Points are how you got there.

payload.prompt: World rankings stay frozen all season. True?

choices.label: No, they move as results come in

explanation.correct: Rankings shift as new results are counted, which is why a big win can jump a player up.
explanation.incorrect: Rankings are not frozen. They are updated as results come in, so a strong event moves a player and a weak one can drop her.
explanation.sayThisLine: Win big at a slam and your ranking moves.

payload.prompt: Complete the ranking statement.
payload.template: A pro's world ranking depends on {{metric}}, and it changes {{frequency}}.

explanation.correct: Rankings track tournament results and update as new results come in.
explanation.incorrect: World rankings are built from tournament results and points, and they update as new results arrive.
explanation.sayThisLine: Ranking means results. Win big and it moves.
